import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 973

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/973](https://www.erdosproblems.com/973)
- [Er92f] Erdős, L., On some problems of {P}. Turán concerning power sums of
  complex numbers. Acta Math. Hungar. (1992), 11--24.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
- [Tu84b] Turán, Paul, On a new method of analysis and its applications. (1984), xvi+584.
-/

open Finset Filter

namespace Erdos973

/--
Does there exist a constant $C>1$ such that, for every $n\geq 2$, there exists a sequence
$z_i\in \mathbb{C}$ with $z_1=1$ and $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$ with
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert < C^{-n}$?

This is Problem 7.3 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
          z 1 = 1 ∧
          (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) ∧
          (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős proved (as described on p.35 of [Tu84b]) that such a sequence does exist with
$\lvert z_i\rvert\leq 1$. Indeed, Erdős' construction gives a value of $C\approx 1.32$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.le_one :
    ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
        z 1 = 1 ∧
        (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z i‖ ≤ 1) ∧
        (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
In [Er92f] (a different) Erdős refines this analysis, proving that if
$M_2=\min_{z_j} \max_{2\leq k\leq n+1} \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq j\leq n}z_j^k\right\rvert$
where the minimum is taken over all $z_j\in \mathbb{C}$ with $\max \lvert z_j\rvert=1$, then
$(1.746)^{-n} < M_2 < (1.745)^{-n}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.m2_bounds :
    ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∀ M_2 : ℝ,
      IsGLB { M | ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
        (∀ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ ≤ 1) ∧
        (∃ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ = 1) ∧
        (∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), M = ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ k‖ ∧
          ∀ m ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ m‖ ≤ M) } M_2 →
      (1.746 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) < M_2 ∧ M_2 < (1.745 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Tang notes in the comments that Theorem 6.1 of [Tu84b] implies that, if $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$
for all $i$, then
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert \geq (2e)^{-(1+o(1))n}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.tang :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ z : ℕ → ℂ,
      (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) →
      ∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1),
        ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ ≥
        (2 * Real.exp 1) ^ (-(1 + f n) * (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos973

findings.description: The bounds are asserted for every n ≥ 2, rather than for sufficiently large n. The upper bound is false already at n = 2. For any admissible pair a,b, relabel so that ‖a‖ = 1 and ‖b‖ ≤ 1. The identity 2a⁴ = (a²−ab−b²)(a²+b²) + (a+b)(a³+b³), followed by the triangle inequality, shows that max(‖a²+b²‖, ‖a³+b³‖) ≥ 2/5. Thus the set in the IsGLB premise has an existing greatest lower bound at least 2/5, whereas 1.745⁻² = 40000/121801 < 2/5. The negation of the stated all-n bound was proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean (not_stated_m2_bounds).
findings.source_evidence: Quanyu Tang’s comment of 10 October 2025, https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/973#post-981, explicitly attributes to [Er92f] estimates holding “for sufficiently large n,” and then states: “For n > n_0, we also have ... 1/(1.746^n) < M_2 < 1/(1.745^n).” The abbreviated remark on the main problem page omits this qualification.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 →` with `∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,`, retaining the remaining GLB predicate and bounds. Alternatively, quantify an eventual threshold N ≥ 2. Update the docstring to say that the bounds hold for all sufficiently large n.

reformulations.difference: Uses a function ℕ → ℂ for each finite sequence and pointwise inequalities over the power range instead of an explicit maximum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each n, only coordinates in [1,n] matter. Restriction to that finite index type and arbitrary extension back to ℕ preserve the normalization, modulus conditions, and sums. Crucially, z is quantified after n, so no single infinite sequence must work for every n. Since [2,n+1] is finite and nonempty for n ≥ 2, its maximum is below the bound exactly when every indexed value is below it. The restriction/extension and finite-maximum equivalences were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Expresses the asymptotic lower bound using an explicit error sequence f, eventual quantification, and an index witnessing the lower bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For real-valued f, `f =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ 1)` is equivalent to f tending to zero. Eventual quantification on ℕ means all n beyond some threshold, and a lower bound on a finite nonempty maximum is equivalent to the existence of an index meeting it. These equivalences were checked in Lean. Uniformity in z agrees with Tang’s quoted quantitative estimate n·(n/(2e(n+1)))^n, which depends only on n.

Local STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean; relevant Mathlib definitions and lemmas for intervals, finite extrema, complex norms, real powers, IsGLB, little-o, and atTop; supplied calibration examples.
review.notes: All four declarations were checked. The IsGLB encoding itself is sound: its set is nonempty and bounded below for every permitted n, and the minimum is attained by compactness after restricting to finite tuples. Lean boundary tests and the certified refutation are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the refutation depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, not on the reviewed sorry declarations. Full texts of [Er92f], [Ha74], and [Tu84b] were not obtained; the relevant numerical and Turán estimates were read in the source’s explicit quotations. No additional mathematical defects or status mismatches were found.

not_demonstrated.reason: The existing certified disproof requires a uniform lower bound over all normalized complex pairs, using a polynomial identity and norm inequalities, followed by establishing and bounding the GLB. This is a mathematical argument, not a handful-line computation or trivial counterexample; I could not shorten it to the requested standard without hiding substantial supporting proofs.

submission.summary: The previously reported misformalization remains substantiated by the longer scratch proof, but no trivial-proof demonstration is submitted. No trivial_proof.lean file remains.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole finding concerns an infimum over complex configurations. Even at n = 2, disproving the statement requires the substantive uniform lower-bound argument, rather than merely evaluating a concrete configuration. The existing proof exceeds this task’s explicit triviality requirement.

submission.summary: Changed the numerical bounds to hold for all sufficiently large n using `∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop`, and updated the docstring accordingly. No other declarations were changed. The requested compilation succeeded with only the existing `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
